package terminal // import "ubunatic.com/loom/terminal"

Package terminal provides safe, unified, idempotent terminal mode restoration
for loom commands, panes, and external tools that enter raw mode.

CONSTANTS

const ResetAltScreen = "\x1b[?1049l"
    ResetAltScreen is the ANSI sequence to exit the alternate screen buffer.

const ResetKittyKeyboard = "\x1b[<u"
    ResetKittyKeyboard is the ANSI sequence to pop the Kitty keyboard protocol
    state.

const ResetSequences = "\x1b[?9l" +
	"\x1b[?1000l" +
	"\x1b[?1002l" +
	"\x1b[?1003l" +
	"\x1b[?1005l" +
	"\x1b[?1006l" +
	"\x1b[?1015l" +
	"\x1b[?1004l" +
	"\x1b[?2004l" +
	"\x1b[r" +
	"\x1b[0m" +
	"\x1b[?25h" +
	"\x1b[0 q" +
	"\x1b[?7h"
    ResetSequences contains the ANSI escape sequence string that resets every
    terminal mode a child or loom process may set: mouse tracking (9, 1000,
    1002, 1003, 1005, 1006, 1015 off), focus events (1004 off), bracketed
    paste (2004 off), DECSTBM scroll region reset (r), SGR reset (0m), cursor
    visibility (25h), default cursor shape (0 q), and auto-wrap on (7h).


FUNCTIONS

func DrainInput(fd int)
    DrainInput flushes the terminal input queue (TCIFLUSH) so raw-mode leftovers
    do not bleed into the outer shell or subsequent terminal readers.

func Reset(altScreen bool, kittyPop ...bool) string
    Reset returns ResetSequences, plus ResetKittyKeyboard if kittyPop is true,
    and ResetAltScreen if altScreen is true.

func Restore(fd int, state *term.State, out io.Writer, altScreen bool, kittyPop ...bool) error
    Restore writes the full reset sequence set to out, drains unread input
    on fd, and restores state using term.Restore. It is safe to call with an
    invalid or non-terminal fd (such as in tests).


TYPES

type Restorer struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Restorer manages terminal cleanup hooks, alternate screen state, and
    signals. It ensures that terminal restoration is thread-safe and strictly
    idempotent.

func NewRestorer(fd int, state *term.State, out io.Writer) *Restorer
    NewRestorer constructs a Restorer for the given terminal file descriptor and
    output writer.

func (r *Restorer) AltScreen() bool
    AltScreen reports whether the alternate screen buffer exit is enabled.

func (r *Restorer) CatchSignals(onSignal func(os.Signal), sigs ...os.Signal)
    CatchSignals configures the Restorer to listen for the provided signals.
    If any received signal is caught, onSignal is invoked (if non-nil),
    Restore() is executed, and r exits or hands control back.

func (r *Restorer) OnRestore(fn func())
    OnRestore registers a hook to be run during restoration before mode reset.

func (r *Restorer) Restore()
    Restore runs all registered cleanup hooks, writes reset sequences, drains
    input, and restores terminal cooked state. Restore is idempotent.

func (r *Restorer) SetAltScreen(on bool)
    SetAltScreen configures whether Restore will exit the alternate screen
    buffer.

func (r *Restorer) SetKittyKeyboard(on bool)
    SetKittyKeyboard configures whether Restore will pop the Kitty keyboard
    protocol.

func (r *Restorer) StopSignals()
    StopSignals unregisters the signal handler.
